data.body:
PRIOR-ART SEARCH — this is NOT a regression. Two earlier fixes in the same subsystem were checked and
BOTH are verifiably still in place. Recording this so nobody re-derives it, and — more importantly —
so nobody tries to fix this one the way those were fixed, because that approach cannot work here.

SEARCHED: "no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event", "plan_relation_snapshot_error", "reducer-error",
"empty ticket directory", "plan relation snapshot failed".

CANDIDATE 1 — fa77-b035-8541-4763 (CLOSED) "Plan relation snapshots reject rebar runtime marker files".
Closest match by subsystem. It fixed per-ticket `.archived` and `.write.lock` runtime markers making
the store permanently git-DIRTY, so `tracker_head_sha` rejected it and every plan review returned an
unsigned INDETERMINATE store-read-failure. Remedy: add those patterns to the tickets-branch gitignore.
VERIFIED STILL IN PLACE: `*/.archived` and `*/.write.lock` are both present in the tickets-branch
`.gitignore`; the markers exist on disk (e.g. `f2dc-cfff-cf06-483e/.write.lock`, `.../.archived`);
`git status --porcelain` on the tracker is CLEAN. Not regressed.

CANDIDATE 2 — c083-4d7d-0aca-4e3f (CLOSED) "sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files:
attest.py omits ignore_untracked". Same theme, git-visibility again.
VERIFIED STILL IN PLACE: `ignore_untracked` is present at
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:208,212,242`. Not regressed.

WHY NEITHER FIX COULD EVER HAVE COVERED THIS, and why the gitignore route is a dead end here:
both prior fixes work by making git IGNORE an artifact it can otherwise SEE. Git cannot track empty
directories at all — an event-less ticket directory never appears in `git status`, never reaches the
tickets branch, and cannot be gitignored because there is nothing for git to ignore. Confirmed
directly: with the two orphan directories present, `git status --porcelain` was clean and the failure
still occurred. So this is a different failure mode reached by a different path — the REDUCER walking
the store directory listing, not git reporting dirtiness — and it needs a fix in the reducer, not in
`.gitignore`.

THE PATTERN WORTH NAMING: three separate tickets now (fa77, c083, this one) all reduce to "the
plan-review path is intolerant of store detritus and fails closed on an unrelated ticket". Each was
fixed for its specific artifact. Whoever takes this one should consider whether the reducer should
tolerate ANY unreadable/incomplete store entry by skipping it with a named warning, rather than
accruing a fourth case-by-case fix.
